explanation: Vertebrates possess the same 4 chordate characteristics as nonvertebrates in their embryonic stages, but additionally share: 1) a Vertebral column that replaces the embryonic notochord; 2) a Skull enclosing the brain and sensory organs; 3) an Endoskeleton of living tissue that grows with the organism, protecting organs and anchoring muscles; and 4) complex Internal organs (large coelom, complete digestive tract, closed circulatory system, lungs or gills, and separate sexes reproducing sexually). Evolutionarily, vertebrates began with jawless fish, followed by jawed fish. Amphibians were the first terrestrial organisms with limbs, reproducing in water. Reptiles were the first to fully adapt to land, developing amniotic eggs and watertight skin. Birds and mammals evolved further from reptilian lineages.

questions.q: What replaces the embryonic notochord in adult vertebrates?
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Vertebral column – replaces the notochord'.

questions.q: Which group was the first to fully adapt to land, developing watertight skin and amniotic eggs?
questions.exp: According to the notes, 'Reptiles first fully adapted to land, and first organisms to have amniotic eggs. Also have watertight skin'.

questions.q: What is unique about a vertebrate endoskeleton compared to arthropod exoskeletons?
opts: It is made of chitin and must be shed periodically.
It is a living tissue that grows with the organism.
It completely lacks bone or cartilage.
It is secreted outside the epithelial cells.
